title: Hot or Cold? How Animals Stay Cool for Kids
description:
How do animals stay cool on a hot day? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out: an elephant flaps its big ears and sprays water and mud on its wrinkly skin, a koala stretches out its arms and legs when it is hot and folds them in when it is cold, and a big tiger cools off by lying in a shady pool.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: African elephant: large ear surface area with networks of blood vessels close to the skin surface allow heat to leave the body; flapping the ears dissipates a lot of body heat; wrinkles help the skin retain moisture, and water and mud adhere to wrinkly skin, which boosts evaporative cooling; elephants spray dust, grass and water on the body; they walk on tiptoes with large fat pads cushioning the feet; they may detect vibrations through their feet (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'African Elephants', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/african_elephant/characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

Koala: posture changes help with body temperature regulation; on hot days they extend their limbs, and in cold, wet, windy weather they fold their arms and legs in; arboreal, but must travel on the ground to move to another tree; males produce low-frequency bellows; koalas spend most of their time alone (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Koala', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 16 2026).

Tiger: larger subspecies often regulate body temperature by lying partially submerged in shaded pools; active both day and night; sounds include grunting, miaowing, woofing, growling, hissing and prusten or chuffing (gentle puffing); both sexes scent-mark their territories (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Tiger', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 16 2026). Stripes on body, limbs, head and tail (same library, Physical Characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about how animals stay cool!
What do animals do on a hot, hot day?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Fan your face, and let's go!

segments.name: elephant

lines.t: Who flaps big ears, to cool down?
Is it the elephant? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the elephant!
Here is the fun fact. An elephant's big ears help it cool down.
The elephant flaps its ears, and lets the heat out. Flap, flap! Flap, flap!

lines.t: What else helps an elephant cool down? Hmm.

lines: Water and mud! It sprays water and mud on its body. Splash!
Look at its wrinkly skin.
close:elephant
Water and mud stick to the wrinkles, and that helps the elephant stay cool. Nice and cool!
And here is a surprise. Elephants walk on their tiptoes! A soft pad cushions each foot.
An elephant may even feel the ground rumble, through its feet!
Stomp, stomp! Can you feel it? Rumble, rumble!
Say it with me. Elephants flap their ears to cool down!
close:host
Can you flap like an elephant? Put your hands by your ears. Flap, flap!
Now spray water like a trunk. Splash, splash!

lines.t: Quick check! What does an elephant flap, to cool down? Its ears? Or its feet?

lines: Its ears! Flap, flap. Great job!

short.title: Why Does an Elephant Flap Its Big Ears?

segments.name: koala

lines.t: On a hot day, who stretches out its arms and legs, to cool down?
Is it the koala? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the koala!
Here is the fun fact. On a hot day, a koala stretches out its arms and legs.
Stretch, stretch! That helps it cool down.

lines.t: What does a koala do on a cold, windy day? Hmm.

lines: It folds its arms and legs in, and makes itself small. Snuggle!
Snug as can be! A cozy, little ball of fur.
close:koala
A koala spends most of its time up in the trees.
But to get to another tree, it climbs down, and walks on the ground. Step, step, step!
Boy koalas can make a very low, loud call. It is called a bellow!
A koala mostly likes to be alone, up in its own tree.
Say it with me. A koala stretches out when it is hot!
close:host
Can you cool down like a koala? Stretch out your arms and legs!
Now it is cold. Fold your arms and legs in. Snuggle!

lines.t: Quick check! On a hot day, what does a koala do? Stretch out? Or curl up?

lines: Stretch out! You remembered!

short.title: How Does a Koala Cool Down on a Hot Day?

segments.name: tiger

lines.t: Which big cat cools off, by lying in a shady pool of water?
Is it the tiger? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the tiger!
Here is the fun fact. On a hot day, big tigers often cool off by lying in a shady pool.
Just part of the tiger is in the water. Ahh, nice and cool!

lines.t: Is a tiger busy in the day, or at night? Hmm.

lines: Both! Tigers can be busy in the day, and at night too.
A tiger can be awake any time.
close:tiger
Tigers make lots of sounds. Growls, and grunts, and even a miaow!
One gentle tiger sound is called chuffing. It is a soft, puffing sound. Puff, puff!
Every tiger has stripes on its body, its legs, its head and its tail.
A tiger leaves its smell on trees, to say: this is my home!
Say it with me. A tiger cools off in a shady pool!
close:host
Can you lie down like a tiger in a cool pool? Ahh!
Now chuff like a tiger. Puff, puff, puff!

lines.t: Quick check! Where does a big tiger cool off? In a shady pool? Or in the snow?

lines: In a shady pool! Nice and cool. Super thinking!

short.title: How Does a Tiger Cool Off? Tiger Facts for Kids

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three friends who know how to stay cool. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who flaps big ears to cool down?
Who stretches out its arms and legs on a hot day?
Who cools off in a shady pool?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Flap like an elephant. Stretch like a koala. And chuff like a tiger!
How do you cool down on a hot day?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
